video_title: How Tokenized Stocks Could Undercut Interactive Brokers' 77% Profit Margin
gist: Alex Cutler, CEO of Dromos Labs (the team behind Aerodrome on Base), argues Coinbase's newly launched tokenized Apple, Nvidia, Meta and Google tokens are the first tokenized equities with true 1:1 share backing and beneficial ownership, and that onchain AMM spot pools — not brokers or perp/RFQ dealer venues — will become the price-discovery layer for equities. He cites early data (~25% of cross-venue AMM volume on these assets, ~$80M since launch, 5,000 holder wallets, onchain NVDA repricing above the close after earnings) and frames the trade as disintermediating incumbents like Interactive Brokers and their ~77% profit margin.

themes.theme: Real share backing vs. synthetic wrappers

insights.claim: Coinbase's tokenized Apple, Nvidia, Meta and Google tokens on Base are each backed one-to-one by an actual share held in trust by a regulated custodian, using the same mint-and-redeem mechanism as traditional ETFs — structurally different from the earlier synthetic, debt-claim or derivative-wrapper versions of tokenized equities.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler, CEO and co-founder of Dromos Labs
insights.so_what: Structure is the differentiator to underwrite: only 1:1 custodied designs can plausibly trade at parity and support lending/collateral use, so investors should read the token's terms before treating any tokenized stock as equity exposure.
insights.quote: it's backed one by one by an actual share and it's uh trusted and issued by a regulated custodian

insights.claim: The stablecoin market is offered as the precedent template: consolidation accrued to the stablecoins that genuinely represent the underlying asset and are trivially convertible between the real and digital form, implying the same winner-take-most dynamic will play out in tokenized equities.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: A reusable screen for any tokenized real-world asset: redeemability for the real thing, not distribution or first-mover status, is the predictor of which issuer wins the liquidity.
insights.quote: we've seen such consolidation in stable coins amongst the stable coins that do fundamentally represent the underlying thing

insights.claim: Dividends and stock splits on these tokenized shares are handled through an off-chain multiplier rather than by changing the onchain token supply, so a non-KYC holder still captures the economic value because authorized participants realize the multiplier at mint and redeem.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: The multiplier mechanic means the onchain token price should not be compared naively to the raw underlying share price around corporate actions — a source of apparent basis that is actually accounting, not mispricing.
insights.quote: what they have is an off-chain multiplier

insights.claim: Within the first few days of the Coinbase tokenized-stock launch, Aerodrome captured roughly 25% of all AMM volume in these tokenized assets across every exchange, chain and issuer, doing about $25 million in a 24-hour window and roughly $80 million since launch, with about 5,000 wallets already holding the tokens.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: A concrete, checkable baseline for tracking whether tokenized-equity volume is compounding or was a launch-week novelty; venue concentration this early favors the incumbent AMM capturing the fee stream.
insights.quote: we have captured about 25% of the AMM volumes on these tokenized assets across all exchanges and chains and issuers

insights.claim: Cutler frames the equities push as an extension of a repeatable playbook: Aerodrome on Base already claims to do more volume in Bitcoin markets in many weeks than every other chain and exchange combined, and to lead onchain FX volume — the same dominance he expects to replicate in tokenized stocks.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: If the pattern holds, liquidity in each new onchain asset class concentrates on one dominant venue quickly, so early venue share is the metric to watch rather than total category volume.

themes.theme: Onchain price discovery and oracle risk

insights.claim: After Nvidia reported earnings with US markets closed, millions of dollars of volume flowed into the onchain Nvidia pool on Base and pushed the token's price above the official close — an observed instance of onchain markets acting as the after-hours price-discovery venue for a US equity.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: Onchain equity pools become a free, public after-hours sentiment signal around earnings — tradeable in themselves and readable as an indicator ahead of the cash open.
insights.quote: the price rising higher than the close

insights.claim: Cutler takes the contrarian position that price dislocation from the underlying while traditional markets are closed is the feature rather than the bug of onchain equity markets — but only because the token is a genuine one-to-one claim, which makes the dislocation real price discovery rather than a broken peg.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: Reframes weekend basis from an arbitrage-and-risk problem into an information product; it also means investors should not assume dislocations will mean-revert to the close.
insights.quote: price dislocations when markets are closed is the feature not the bug

insights.claim: Cutler predicts that oracles for tokenized equities will migrate away from off-chain feeds of exchange closing prices toward the liquidation prices observable in onchain AMM pools, with Chainlink said to be working on 24/7 feeds — making deep spot AMM liquidity the prerequisite for tokenized-equity lending markets to scale.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: Whoever hosts the deepest spot pool becomes the de facto pricing authority for tokenized-equity collateral — a durable moat and a systemic dependency worth monitoring.
insights.quote: the oracle will not be some off-chain connection between the NASDAQ and uh you know, these onchain markets

insights.claim: Laura Shin flags the concrete failure mode the guest does not fully resolve: a 24/5 oracle tracking an underlying that does not trade on weekends, combined with thinner weekend onchain liquidity, can let the token price dislocate materially and create problems for collateralized positions by Monday morning.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (host)
insights.so_what: The first real stress test for tokenized-equity DeFi is likely a weekend gap event; lending protocols accepting these tokens as collateral carry oracle-and-liquidity risk that is not yet priced.

insights.claim: The disintermediation pitch is explicitly aimed at brokerage economics: Cutler says Interactive Brokers extracts roughly a 77% profit margin on the activity of routing international investors into US equities, and claims onchain spot markets have already at moments delivered better execution than that incumbent.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: Frames listed brokers serving non-US retail as the margin pool being attacked; the metric to watch is whether onchain execution quality on tokenized stocks holds up as size grows.
insights.quote: it extracts you know a staggering like 77% profit margin on that type of activity

insights.claim: Nine DeFi protocols were integrated at launch — including Aerodrome, Morpho, Euler, 0x, 1inch, Kyber Swap, CoW Swap and Wasabi — which Cutler argues makes a composable, programmable tokenized share not merely a better tokenized stock but a better stock than the traditional instrument.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: If composability (collateral, leverage, automated portfolios) is the real product differentiator, the value accrues to the DeFi money-legos layer rather than to the issuer, and adoption should be tracked in lending/collateral TVL, not just spot volume.
insights.quote: this is not just a um you know better version of a tokenized stock at this point. This is a better version of a stock period

insights.claim: New structured products are already stacking on top of the tokenized shares: Arcadia has launched leveraged LP positions, Bitwise built an automated token portfolio that removes the fund wrapper and keeps assets in the user's wallet, Reserve launched a tokenized Mag 7 basket, and Centrifuge is migrating liquidity from another DEX to Aerodrome.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: Wrapper-free onchain index and basket products are a direct competitive threat to ETF fee structures, and the named builders are the early observable cohort of that attack.

insights.claim: The animating framework is that permissionless market making democratizes the market-maker role the way the internet democratized filmmaking — retail participants providing liquidity onchain can capture fee income that in traditional equities accrues to professional market makers of the kind Ken Griffin runs.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: If liquidity provision genuinely opens up, market-making spread income becomes a retail-accessible yield source and a structural headwind to the economics of incumbent equity market makers.
insights.quote: what these markets are going to allow people to do is anyone can now be Ken Griffin

themes.theme: US regulatory path and the SEC exemption

insights.claim: These tokenized stocks are currently unavailable to US users, and Cutler expects the eventual SEC framework to split the experience: the tokens themselves stay permissionless and composable across DeFi, while full shareholder benefits such as voting Apple shares would require KYC through Coinbase.com.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: A two-tier design would preserve DeFi composability for the token while pushing governance and full rights into the regulated venue — bullish for Coinbase's funnel and for onchain liquidity, if it lands that way.

insights.claim: Citing leaks and public channels, Cutler believes the SEC already has substantial guidance on tokenized US equities ready to release but is timing it against whether market-structure legislation passes, implying possible gamesmanship in the delay.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: Ties the tokenized-equity regulatory catalyst to the legislative calendar rather than the SEC's own timetable — watch the bill, not the agency, for the unlock date.
insights.quote: they've been waiting for Clarity. And perhaps there's some gamemanship even here

insights.claim: Laura Shin's contrarian read is that even if Coinbase's SEC innovation exemption is granted, US users would likely need a separately designed token, and that the compliant US version could end up being an inferior, more DeFi-restricted product than the one launched offshore.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (host)
insights.so_what: Tempers the bull case: US approval may not translate into US access to the composable version, so growth in tokenized equities may keep coming from non-US flow.
insights.quote: it might have to be an inferior product to the one that was launched

insights.claim: Aerodrome redistributes 100% of protocol revenue to holders of its token, so fees generated by tokenized-equity trading — already tens of thousands of dollars within days of launch — flow directly to token holders rather than to equity holders of a corporate operator.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: Creates a direct, measurable linkage between tokenized-stock volume growth and the token's cash flows, making venue market share a quantifiable valuation input.
insights.quote: we redistribute 100% of the protocol's revenue right back to users of the token

insights.claim: Cutler cites Brian Armstrong's claim that Coinbase expects 10% of global GDP to come onchain within five years — dismissed as far-fetched when made on an earnings call during the bear market — as newly plausible given the adoption rate of tokenized equities, and says Aerodrome will also launch on Circle's ARC chain to push onchain FX growth.
insights.speaker: Alex Cutler
insights.so_what: Signals where the venue expands next: FX on a stablecoin-issuer chain is the second front after equities, and Circle's ARC becomes a place to watch for onchain FX volume migration.
insights.quote: in the next five years, we will bring 10% of global GDP onchain
